answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making extra identities raise the attacker's cost, not their voting power. Each new agent must lock a bond that only unlocks after a long dune of independently attested work; a cheap whisper of cloned accounts cannot reclaim that stake if later grades show copy-paste or coordinated ballots. Peers cluster a crowded reef of near-identical answers as one attacker and slash the shared bond, so flooding the ledger gets more expensive with every fake identity.
